title: quest task view <id> --ref <ref>: read a task at a git ref
description: Filed under DEC-206 (c3) (opum-doc dev b20f5979, opum-ai/opum-doc#1129). Reading a task at a ref is a missing Quest capability. The consumer is opum-cli OCLI-243 piece 3(a): opum-cli must never read .quest/ through git show, because hand-parsing private storage is the coupling its profile forbids. `quest task view <id> --ref <ref>` reads the task as it exists at that ref and returns the same envelope as `task view`, plus the resolved sha. It is a read, so it carries no revision precondition. It rides the next lore/quest pair (Article 3); until then OCLI-243 compiles from the local tree and names the lag. Not started; filed only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `quest task view <id> --ref <ref>` returns the same envelope shape as `task view <id>`, with the commit sha the ref resolved to added to it
The command carries no revision precondition and writes nothing
A task present only at the ref (absent from the working tree) resolves, and an id absent at the ref fails with a named not_found rather than a bare error
An unresolvable ref fails with a distinct, named error
Proven both ways: a test that reads at a ref and gets the record, and one that mutates the ref handling and goes red

plan: 1. Read the task: new --ref flag on task view, same envelope plus resolved sha, no revision precondition, named not_found for missing id and a distinct error for an unresolvable ref.

2. Implement readTaskAtRef in src/application/tasks/read-at-ref.ts: resolve the ref to a sha, list .quest/{tasks,completed,archive/tasks} at that sha via listFilesRequired, parse+validate each record, resolve id or alias with the same findTask the working-tree read uses, return task+path+recordRevision+sha. Four named errors: ref_not_resolvable, task_not_found, ref_records_unreadable, ref_record_duplicate.

3. Wire --ref into the task view branch of src/cli/main.ts: carry {ref, sha} as an additive top-level envelope key between data and principal (contractVersion index and principal-last preserved); reuse withNoteCap (extracted from the command layer) and the existing --fields projection so both compose.
4. Declare the flag in command-contract.ts filters and command-help.ts (summary, usage, flags).

5. Tests in test/qcli519-task-view-at-ref.test.ts on a real git fixture: ref-only task resolves; same id differs between ref and working tree; case-insensitive id; missing id = task_not_found; unresolvable ref = ref_not_resolvable; nothing written; no revision precondition; --max-notes/--fields compose.
6. Mutation proof: point the listing at HEAD instead of the resolved sha and confirm the predicted subset goes red, then restore.
7. Run bun run check with the pinned bun, commit on feat/QCLI-519-task-view-ref, push, open the PR, report the head SHA.
implementationNotes: Implementation note, 2026-10-21. readTaskAtRef lives at src/application/tasks/read-at-ref.ts; it lists the three task locations at the resolved sha with listFilesRequired (strict), so a failed listing is ref_records_unreadable (exit 6) rather than an empty ref. The envelope extra is a top-level `ref` object {ref, sha} emitted after `data` and before `principal`, which keeps contractVersion at index 1 and principal last (QCLI-289/QCLI-316 slot rule). Three consumer surfaces needed the new filter in the same change: command-contract.ts (the manifest), src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts and src/contract/tracker/index.ts (the packaged tracker client compares filters by exact equality, so a manifest that grows one without it fails every probe closed), plus the inline manifest golden in test/contract/command-contract.test.ts. MUTATION CONTROL for AC5: changing the listing revision from the resolved sha to HEAD turned 4 of 9 tests red (the four ref-reading ones) and left the 5 negative controls green -- the predicted subset; restored, all 9 pass. bun run check exits 0 on bun 1.4.2 (1275 tests, 0 fail).

Round-1 review fixes in e9ec032d on feat/QCLI-519-task-view-ref. MAJOR: --ref now resolves the ref as <ref>^{commit}; an annotated tag reports the commit it peels to, and a tree-ish or blob-ish is ref_not_resolvable (exit 3) instead of a false tree-damage read. MINOR 1: findTask re-throws everything except task_not_found, so task_reference_ambiguous is a conflict (exit 5), the same outcome the working-tree view gives. MINOR 2: input.code carries task_not_found or ref_not_resolvable. MINOR 4: both exit-6 modes now have tests -- the listing failure and the duplicate id with input.paths. MINOR 5: a CHANGELOG Added entry. MINOR 6: the plain form ends with a ref footer. NIT: ListingExtras renamed EnvelopeExtras, and the overview guide names --ref.
MUTATION EVIDENCE, re-measured by the session that pushed rather than relayed. (a) MAJOR, both ways: reverting the ^{commit} peel reddens exactly 2 of 15 -- the annotated-tag case and the tree-ish/blob-ish case -- and the unmutated build is 15 pass / 0 fail. (b) MINOR 3 CORRECTED COUNT: under the recorded mutation (the listing revision sha replaced by HEAD while blobs are still read at the resolved sha) the round-1 nine-test suite goes 3 pass / 6 fail -- items at :139, :151, :183, :188, :202 and :229 -- and the current fifteen-test suite goes 10 pass / 5 fail, the same four plus the new plain-footer case. So the earlier 4-of-9 note was an UNDERCOUNT and the reviewer prediction of at least 5 was closer: the true count is 6. The reviewer also predicted :171 would go red and it does not -- :171 survives this mutation, because only the listing moves to HEAD while blob content still comes from the resolved sha -- so the corrected figure is 6 of 9 with :171 explicitly green, not 4 and not 5. The implementer report attributing :188 and :202 to a stronger resolved-ref mutation does not reproduce: both are red under the recorded listing mutation as measured here.

Round-2 FULL review recorded on head ceb5beff (unit quest-cli-review-656r2, model deepseek-flash, DEC-183 Stage 1, read-only): APPROVE. Every AC passed; round-1 MAJOR-1 and MINOR 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and NIT-8 were marked RESOLVED with file:line. Both exit-6 tests go red under their own mutations (listing swap gives exit 3, duplicate check removed gives exit 5). No argv injection: --ref=--foo is exit 3, --ref --foo is exit 2. PR merged to dev as 99e8980f. Three NITs remain, filed as one To Do task; none is worked here.

CORRECTION to my previous note on this task, which claimed the recorded listing mutation turns 6 of the round-1 nine red (:139 :151 :183 :188 :202 :229). THAT MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG and is withdrawn. It ran the ROUND-1 TEST FILE against the ROUND-1-PLUS-FIXES SOURCE, so two of its reds were not the mutation at all: the absent-id and unresolvable-ref cases pin input exactly as {ref} and went red because MINOR 2 added input.code. Re-measured with both halves at round 1 (source and tests both from 74eceefb, only the listing revision changed from sha to HEAD): 9 tests, 4 fail / 5 pass. The four reds, by NAME: "a task present only at the ref resolves there, and is absent in the working tree"; "the envelope carries the same shape plus ref provenance, with principal last"; "an alias-or-id match is case-insensitive, the same resolver task view uses"; "--max-notes and --fields compose with --ref". The reviewer static analysis and the implementer count were both right, and the finalSummary 4-red/5-green figure is correct and now consistent with the notes. On the CURRENT fifteen-test suite the same mutation is 5 fail / 10 pass: the same four plus the new plain-footer case.
finalSummary: Delivered on feat/QCLI-519-task-view-ref: `quest task view <id> --ref <ref>` reads a task at a git ref (DEC-206 c3), returning the same data shape as the working-tree read plus an additive top-level `ref` {ref, sha} between data and principal. New src/application/tasks/read-at-ref.ts with four named failures: ref_not_resolvable and task_not_found (exit 3, deliberately distinct), ref_records_unreadable and ref_record_duplicate (exit 6 drift, so an unreadable tree never reads as an empty ref). It does not fetch, writes nothing, and carries no revision precondition. --max-notes (via the extracted withNoteCap) and --fields compose unchanged. The packaged tracker client grew `ref` in its exact-equality manifest expectation in the same change. Evidence: test/qcli519-task-view-at-ref.test.ts on real Git fixtures (9/9 pass), mutation control replacing the resolved sha with HEAD turns 4 ref-reading tests red while the 5 negative controls stay green, and bun run check exits 0 on bun 1.4.2 (1275 tests, 0 fail).
